title: Laparoscopic ovarian cyst removal
what: Through a few small cuts in your belly, the surgeon removes the cyst and carefully keeps the healthy ovary tissue. It is done under general anesthesia.
why: When a cyst does not go away on its own, grows, causes pain, or looks unclear on ultrasound.
duration: surgery usually takes 40 to 90 minutes, with 1 to 2 days in hospital; lab results come in 1 to 2 weeks
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will say what to stop and when
Heart or lung disease, or diabetes

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, an ultrasound, and sometimes tumor marker tests. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Cycle day
prepare.text: Surgery is usually planned outside your period. Check with your doctor.

prepare.title: Anesthetist
prepare.text: Before surgery, an anesthetist will talk with you. Tell them about your health and medicines.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food from the night before and no drinks for a few hours. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

bring: Things for a 1 to 2 day hospital stay
steps: On the day, you change, and an IV line is placed
In the operating room, the anesthetist gives anesthesia, and you fall asleep
The surgeon makes 3 to 4 small cuts and inserts a camera and instruments
The cyst is carefully separated from the ovary and removed
The small cuts are stitched or taped
You wake up in the recovery room
feel: Pain at the small cuts. You will get painkillers
Shoulder pain from the gas is common and passes in 1 to 2 days
after: You can usually get up the same day
No heavy lifting for 2 to 4 weeks
No sex, baths, or pools, usually for 2 to 4 weeks. Your doctor will say exactly
Your doctor will explain the lab results
red_flags: A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or severe or worsening belly pain
Dizziness, fainting, or sudden weakness: call emergency services
Redness or pus at the small cuts

faq.a: Usually yes. The surgeon removes only the cyst and protects the healthy tissue.
Usually yes. If you plan a pregnancy, tell your doctor in advance.
Sometimes. Your doctor will tell you how often to have an ultrasound.

reminders.text: Ovary surgery tomorrow. Pack your documents, ultrasound results, and things. Eat and drink only until the time the clinic gave you.
